problems.theorem_title: Finite admitted prime powers divide the actual harmonic denominator
problems.formal_statement:
theorem ZetaNine.HarmonicStability.harmonic_finite_prime_product_dvd (s K N : ℕ) (S : Finset ℕ)
    (hs : 0 < s)
    (hS : ∀ p ∈ S, p.Prime ∧ p ≤ N ∧ N / p ≤ K ∧ K < p ∧
      harmonicExceptionalProduct s K < p) :
    (∏ p ∈ S, p ^ s) ∣ (harmonicPower s N).den := by sorry
problems.natural_language_statement:
Let $s>0$, $K,N\ge0$, and let $S$ be a finite set of primes. Put $H_N^{(s)}=\sum_{j=1}^{N}j^{-s}$ and

$$E_{s,K}=\prod_{k=1}^{K}\left|\operatorname{num}(H_k^{(s)})\right|.$$

Suppose every $p\in S$ satisfies

$$p\le N,\qquad \lfloor N/p\rfloor\le K,\qquad K<p,\qquad E_{s,K}<p.$$

Then the full finite prime-power product divides the reduced positive harmonic denominator:

$$\prod_{p\in S}p^s\mid\operatorname{den}(H_N^{(s)}).$$

All hypotheses refer to the actual finite harmonic prefixes. The explicit exception bound is a sufficient way to exclude their numerator prime factors; it is not a claim that every large prime is automatically a unit. The theorem supplies finite arithmetic and does not assert any asymptotic prime count or denominator growth rate.

problems.source: https://github.com/Anchen0823/zeta9-research-notes/releases/tag/research-2026-10-02; research/harmonic-denominator-stability-2026-10-01.md, sections 1–2, equations (1)–(2) and the finite-prime lower-bound argument preceding equation (3).
problems.explanation: Each admitted prime has $1\le\lfloor N/p\rfloor\le K<p$, hence $N<p^2$. Every possible reduced prefix numerator divides the positive integer $E_{s,K}$. Since $p>E_{s,K}$, that numerator is prime to $p$. Splitting the actual sum into its multiples of $p$ and its nonmultiple remainder gives $v_p(H_N^{(s)})=-s$, so its reduced denominator contains exactly $p^s$. Prime powers associated with distinct members of the finite set are coprime; multiplying these divisors proves the full product divisibility.

problems.theorem_title: Finite prime logarithms bound the actual harmonic log denominator below
problems.formal_statement:
theorem ZetaNine.HarmonicStability.harmonic_finite_prime_log_lower_bound (s K N : ℕ) (S : Finset ℕ)
    (hs : 0 < s)
    (hS : ∀ p ∈ S, p.Prime ∧ p ≤ N ∧ N / p ≤ K ∧ K < p ∧
      harmonicExceptionalProduct s K < p) :
    (s : ℝ) * (∑ p ∈ S, Real.log (p : ℝ)) ≤ logDen (harmonicPower s N) := by sorry
problems.natural_language_statement:
Let $s>0$, $K,N\ge0$, and let $S$ be a finite set of primes. With $H_N^{(s)}=\sum_{j=1}^{N}j^{-s}$ and $E_{s,K}=\prod_{k=1}^{K}|\operatorname{num}(H_k^{(s)})|$, suppose every $p\in S$ satisfies

$$p\le N,\qquad \lfloor N/p\rfloor\le K,\qquad K<p,\qquad E_{s,K}<p.$$

Then

$$s\sum_{p\in S}\log p\le\log\operatorname{den}(H_N^{(s)}).$$

Here the denominator is fully reduced and positive. The finite inequality holds for every admitted finite prime set, including the empty set. It is the arithmetic lower bound before applying the prime number theorem; no asymptotic prime-distribution or full-sequence denominator-rate statement is part of the conclusion.

problems.explanation: The finite-prime product theorem gives the positive divisor $\prod_{p\in S}p^s$ of the actual reduced denominator. Therefore that product is at most the denominator. Take natural logarithms and use the finite identity $\log\prod_{p\in S}p^s=s\sum_{p\in S}\log p$. The positivity needed for logarithmic monotonicity follows from primality and the positive reduced rational denominator.

problems.theorem_title: A unit harmonic prefix forces the exact large-prime denominator exponent
problems.formal_statement:
theorem ZetaNine.HarmonicStability.harmonic_large_prime_den_valuation (s N p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime)
    (hs : 0 < s) (hNp : p ≤ N) (hN : N < p ^ 2)
    (hunit : ¬ p ∣ (harmonicPower s (N / p)).num.natAbs) :
    padicValNat p (harmonicPower s N).den = s := by sorry
problems.natural_language_statement:
Let $s>0$ and $N\ge0$, and let $p$ be prime with $p\le N<p^2$. If $p$ does not divide the reduced numerator of the actual prefix $H_{\lfloor N/p\rfloor}^{(s)}$, then

$$v_p\!\left(\operatorname{den}(H_N^{(s)})\right)=s,\qquad H_N^{(s)}=\sum_{j=1}^{N}j^{-s}.$$

The numerator-unit condition is essential. For example, $H_2^{(9)}=513/512$ has a factor $19$ in its numerator, and for $N=38,p=19$ the actual denominator exponent is eight instead of nine. The theorem concerns the exact reduced positive denominator for each admitted parameter; it does not invoke the prime number theorem.

problems.explanation: Since $N<p^2$, the prefix length $\lfloor N/p\rfloor$ is below $p$, so its denominator is prime to $p$. The numerator hypothesis makes its rational $p$-adic valuation zero. In the exact splitting $H_N^{(s)}=p^{-s}H_{\lfloor N/p\rfloor}^{(s)}+U_{s,N,p}$, the first term has valuation $-s$, while the nonmultiple remainder is $p$-integral. Unequal valuations imply $v_p(H_N^{(s)})=-s$, with zero remainders handled separately. Reducedness then gives precisely exponent $s$ in the positive denominator.
